name: PrayerZone Flutter & Dart Library
description: Powerful Flutter and Dart prayer calculation library and location engine providing 23 astronomical calculation methods with angle configurations (including Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs and Wakfs: Fajr 18°, Isha 17°), 2 juristic Madhabs, and geocoded presets for 182 countries.

authentication.description: Open source client library (MIT License). Runs offline on device without network latency.

platforms: Flutter (Android, iOS, Web, macOS, Windows, Linux)
Pure Dart (CLI, Server / Dart Frog, Backend)

algerianCalculation.authority: Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs and Wakfs
algerianCalculation.schoolNote: Standard shadow length factor 1:1, aligned with the predominant Maliki school of jurisprudence in Algeria
algerianCalculation.description: Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs and Wakfs. Uses standard Fajr angle of 18° and Isha angle of 17°.

calculationMethods.name: Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs and Wakfs
calculationMethods.description: Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs and Wakfs. Uses standard Fajr angle of 18° and Isha angle of 17°.

calculationMethods.name: Muslim World League
calculationMethods.description: Muslim World League. Standard Fajr time with an angle of 18°. Earlier Isha time with an angle of 17°.

calculationMethods.name: Egyptian General Authority of Survey
calculationMethods.description: Egyptian General Authority of Survey. Early Fajr time using an angle 19.5° and a slightly earlier Isha time using an angle of 17.5°.

calculationMethods.name: Union des Organisations Islamiques de France (UOIF)
calculationMethods.description: Union des Organisations Islamiques de France. Uses nautical twilight angles of 12° for both Fajr and Isha, resulting in later Fajr and earlier Isha times.

calculationMethods.name: Gulf Region Convention
calculationMethods.description: Gulf Region convention. Uses a Fajr angle of 19.5° and a fixed 90 minute interval after Maghrib for Isha.

calculationMethods.name: Kementerian Agama Republik Indonesia (KEMENAG)
calculationMethods.description: Kementerian Agama Republik Indonesia (KEMENAG). Used in Indonesia. Early Fajr time with an angle of 20° and standard Isha time with an angle of 18°.

calculationMethods.name: Shia Ithna-Ashari, Leva Institute, Qum
calculationMethods.description: Shia Ithna-Ashari, Leva Institute, Qum. Uses a Fajr angle of 16°, Isha angle of 14°, and calculates Maghrib when the sun reaches 4° below the horizon.

calculationMethods.name: Ministry of Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Places, Jordan
calculationMethods.description: Ministry of Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Places, Jordan. Uses standard Fajr and Isha angles of 18° with a +5 minute Maghrib adjustment.

calculationMethods.name: University of Islamic Sciences, Karachi
calculationMethods.description: University of Islamic Sciences, Karachi. A generally applicable method that uses standard Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

calculationMethods.name: Umm al-Qura University, Makkah
calculationMethods.description: Umm al-Qura University, Makkah. Uses a fixed interval of 90 minutes from maghrib to calculate Isha. And a slightly earlier Fajr time with an angle of 18.5°. Note: you should add a +30 minute custom adjustment for Isha during Ramadan.

calculationMethods.name: Dubai (UAE Convention)
calculationMethods.description: Used in the UAE. Slightly earlier Fajr time and slightly later Isha time with angles of 18.2° for Fajr and Isha in addition to 3 minute offsets for sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, and Maghrib.

calculationMethods.name: Comunidade Islamica de Lisboa
calculationMethods.description: Comunidade Islamica de Lisboa. Uses a standard Fajr angle of 18° with a 77 minute fixed interval for Isha and a +3 minute Maghrib adjustment.

calculationMethods.name: Qatar Convention
calculationMethods.description: Same Isha interval as ummAlQura but with the standard Fajr time using an angle of 18°.

calculationMethods.name: Kuwait Convention
calculationMethods.description: Standard Fajr time with an angle of 18°. Slightly earlier Isha time with an angle of 17.5°.

calculationMethods.name: Moonsighting Committee Worldwide
calculationMethods.description: Method developed by Khalid Shaukat, founder of Moonsighting Committee Worldwide. Uses standard 18° angles for Fajr and Isha in addition to seasonal adjustment values (optional shafaq on parameters). This method automatically applies the 1/7 approximation rule for locations above 55° latitude. Recommended for North America and the UK.

calculationMethods.name: Moroccan Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs
calculationMethods.description: Moroccan Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs. Uses Fajr angle of 19° and Isha angle of 17° with adjustments of -3 for sunrise, +5 for Dhuhr, and +5 for Maghrib.

calculationMethods.name: Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia
calculationMethods.description: Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia. Uses a Fajr angle of 16° and Isha angle of 15°.

calculationMethods.name: Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS)
calculationMethods.description: Used in Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Fajr 20°, Isha 18°, Dhuhr +1 min; minute rounding uses Rounding.up (may differ slightly from older nearest-minute behavior).

calculationMethods.name: Tunisian Ministry of Religious Affairs
calculationMethods.description: Tunisian Ministry of Religious Affairs. Uses standard Fajr and Isha angles of 18°.

calculationMethods.name: Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı (Turkey Approximation)
calculationMethods.description: An approximation of the Diyanet method used in Turkey. This approximation is less accurate outside the region of Turkey.

calculationMethods.name: Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran
calculationMethods.description: Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran. Early Isha time with an angle of 14°. Slightly later Fajr time with an angle of 17.7°. Calculates Maghrib based on the sun reaching an angle of 4.5° below the horizon.

calculationMethods.name: Islamic Society of North America (ISNA)
calculationMethods.description: Also known as the ISNA method. Can be used for North America, but the moonsightingCommittee method is preferable. Gives later Fajr times and early Isha times with angles of 15°.

calculationMethods.name: Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia (JAKIM) / Custom Base
calculationMethods.description: Defaults to angles of 0°, should generally be used for making a custom method and setting your own values.

madhabs.name: Shafi / Maliki / Hanbali
madhabs.description: Earlier Asr time. When an object's shadow equals the length of the object plus shadow at solar noon. Standard in North Africa (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia) and Levant/Southeast Asia.

madhabs.name: Hanafi
madhabs.description: Later Asr time. When an object's shadow equals twice the length of the object plus shadow at solar noon.

staticMethods.name: supportedCountries
staticMethods.description: Returns list of all 182 supported countries with ISO code, name, prayer method, and prayer Madhab.

staticMethods.name: supportedCountriesCount
staticMethods.description: Returns integer count of supported countries (182).

staticMethods.name: getCountry
staticMethods.description: Returns Country metadata for given ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. 'DZ' for Algeria).

staticMethods.name: calculationMethods
staticMethods.description: Returns list of all 23 prayer calculation methods including depression angles and offsets.

staticMethods.name: calculationMethodsCount
staticMethods.description: Returns integer count of calculation methods (23).

staticMethods.name: aboutCalculationMethod
staticMethods.description: Returns detailed metadata for a specific calculation method.
